note.headline: Apple holds at 355.58, still above every value estimate; no new business news

summary.thesis: Apple is a high-quality, cash-rich business, but the price of 355.58 assumes faster growth than it is showing, while forecasts are falling.
summary.decision: Long-term: wait for a lower price. Swing: wait for a breakout or a pullback that holds.
summary.act_at: Long-term buy from 300.56; swing entry only on a close above 361.9

note.happening: Apple closed at 355.58, up 0.43%, in an uptrend and above its 50-day average of 342.84. The only news since the last note is a reported TechCrunch review of the iPhone Duo and a reported Black Friday streaming deals story, and neither affects the numbers. The next earnings report is due on 2027-01-28.
note.business: The business itself is strong. Over the last twelve months, revenue was 478.8B, up from 416.2B, and free cash flow (cash left after running and investing in the business) was 136.1B, up from 98.8B. Operating margin rose to 33.01% from 31.97%. Two things are softening. Growth in the latest quarter slowed to 11.72%, down from 16.6% two quarters ago. And analysts have cut their forecasts: next-quarter earnings per share fell to 2.15 from 2.24, and next-year earnings fell to 10.6 from 10.84. The main risk to the business is inventory. It is up 154% while quarterly sales are up 12%, and unsold product can force price cuts that lower margins. The new investigation risk added to the annual report is a governance and sentiment issue for now, not a demand or margin issue. Cash is not at risk: liquidity is 56.7B, though debt of 80.1B exceeds cash of 36.3B, leaving net cash of -23.4B. Buybacks cut the share count by 1.56% over the year.

worth.text: At 355.58, Apple trades at 39.6 times its past earnings and 33.5 times next year's forecast earnings. It trades at 10.8 times sales, against a peer median of 5.3, which is the highest it has been in its own 5-year history. A discounted cash flow model (today's value of future cash) gives 145.37 in the bear case, 202.38 in the base case and 265.87 in the bull case. Apple's own price-to-sales history gives 222.1 to 300.56. What drives the gap is the assumed growth rate. To justify today's price, free cash flow would have to start growing at about 26.8% a year. At 20% starting growth the value is 273.62, and only at 30% does it reach 400.49. The margin assumption matters too: if operating margin fell to 24%, the value drops to 204.81.
worth.key_assumption: The price needs free cash flow to start growing at about 26.8% a year, well above last year's 15% sales growth.

decision.timing: Options price a 5.1% move by 2026-12-18 and a 10.4% move by 2027-02-19, a window that covers the 2027-01-28 report. There is no long-term buy above 300.56 before that report shows whether the inventory build hurt margins.
